g.text: samtal: may this utterance cancel the reply in flight?
The session marks activity first, whatever
follows: an utterance that ended is somebody
talking, whether or not it earns a reply.
That is what the idle timeout is specified by.
An utterance ended while a reply is streaming
For a board whose echo cancellation leaks its
own voice back. Mic frames are already filtered
upstream in _handle_audio, so what reaches here
The user is holding the button and speaking.
That is a deliberate act, not an acoustic
A noise blip, not an interjection. Only the
endpointer can tell the two apart, which is
why it reports speech_ms at all.
The reply in flight was transcribing the head
of this same sentence. Merging means one reply
answers the whole thing rather than two replies
Answer the merged utterance as one
is the reply still inside ASR?
What the microphone hears just after playback
starts is as likely the onset transient the
board's echo cancellation let through as it is
A pause, not a stop. Audio ceases within a frame
either way; what pausing preserves is the option
of resuming where it left off.
Ask ASR to transcribe the interruption
Resume the paced stream, keep the reply
The pacing clock is shifted by the pause, so the
stream picks up rather than bursting to catch up.
A wrong pause therefore costs one ASR latency,
the paced stream where it stopped
Evidence of user speech, which is the whole rule:
acoustics alone can at most pause a reply, never
The reply is cancelled, the user is answered
Reversible: paused, or merged into one reply
The utterance is dropped, the reply survives
Every branch emits a structured event. Those events are what
the two thresholds get tuned from, and they are the decision
track a session capture writes alongside the stereo WAV, where
channel 0 is the microphone as received and channel 1 is what
was paced out to the speaker. Echo leakage is then a
